clue.text: Feminist pioneer's garments, with some pieces reused

definitions.meaning: the surface reading: the clothes worn by an early campaigner for women's rights
the setter's reading: the eight different letters of garments, rearranged with several of them used more than once, spell the campaigner's name

explanation.surface: A trailblazing feminist's clothes have been patched together from recycled scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: MARGARET SANGER uses exactly the eight different letters of GARMENTS and no others, with A, R, G and E appearing more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Sanger founded the American birth-control movement, an early campaigner for women's reproductive rights.

clue.text: Mother and daughter in Shakespeare rejected head honcho

parts.note: an informal word for mother

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the daughter's name is read backwards

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters

explanation.surface: A mother and daughter from a Shakespeare play turn down the big boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother and daughter in Shakespeare' tempts you to Lear's family as a whole; mother is just the informal two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the person in charge of a business or team, the boss.

clue.text: Fetching confused traveler around one

indicators.note: around places the jumbled letters on either side of the single numeral
confused means mixed up, so the letters of the traveller word get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, in American spelling
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bewildered tourist wanders around but is attractive all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' reads as the adjective attractive; here it is the noun sense, the act of fetching.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrieval is the act of getting something back or bringing it in, a gerund sense of fetching.

clue.text: In the morning, second hand tickled

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning
second-hand goods are used

explanation.surface: Someone touched up a thrift-store find with a feather early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second hand' suggests a clock; it means pre-owned.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickled in the sense of entertained or pleased, as in 'tickled pink', means amused.

clue.text: Émigré is down to adopt a Windows operating system

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: to down food is to eat it
Windows XP is a Microsoft operating system

explanation.surface: A refugee is depressed about having to switch to a version of Windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like sad, as the surface suggests; it means swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat lives outside their native country, which is what an émigré does.

clue.text: Revise memos or include duplicate e-mail for a suburban voter

indicators.note: include means the copy-to marker goes inside the rearranged letters
to revise is to rework a text, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
cc sends a copy of an email to another recipient

explanation.surface: An office instruction to edit some memos or copy someone in when emailing a suburban constituent.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer mom is a middle-class suburban mother, treated by US pollsters as a key swing demographic.

clue.text: Close to avoiding a place where you might gamble with chemical weaponry

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of the letter named, so it is dropped

parts.note: near means close to
the letter removed
Las Vegas, the Nevada gambling city

explanation.surface: Near a casino city, someone is gambling with chemical arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical weapon that attacks the nervous system, such as sarin.

clue.text: Time to put together an inspiration for poets

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is time to assemble something that will inspire poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Term heard at the card table — or in presidential politics

definitions.text: Term heard at the card table
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bridge bid for a contract played without a trump suit
second meaning: a slogan rejecting Donald Trump's 2016 candidacy

explanation.walkthrough: Published in February 2016, during the primaries, when 'No Trump' was a rallying cry against the Republican front-runner.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a no-trump contract has no trump suit; in politics the phrase was an anti-Trump campaign slogan.

clue.text: Pirate's rude eldest child, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means we go by how the words sound when spoken rather than how they are spelt

parts.note: rude is coarse, and the eldest child is the heir

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's firstborn has terrible manners, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a privateer or pirate, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Scoundrel, hero, guerrilla's hostage

indicators.note: a hostage is held captive, so the answer is held within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A villain and a hero are both held captive by a rebel fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled man, a synonym of scoundrel.

clue.text: Quietly move cover in back, e.g.

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, so the cover sits within the next piece
back tells you to read the abbreviation that follows from right to left

parts.note: the abbreviation for 'for example', taken as written
a lid covers a pot or box

explanation.surface: Instructions to slide a protective cover silently into the back of something, such as a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back, e.g.' looks like an example of a body part, but 'back' reverses e.g. and the cover goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide is to move smoothly and silently, without effort or noise.

clue.text: What you would hear at the beginning of a TV show: "The subatomic particle appears with gravity"

definitions.text: What you would hear at the beginning of a TV show

parts.note: taken as written
a meson is a subatomic particle made of a quark and an antiquark
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A physics announcement, as though a programme opened with a line about particles and gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks pretend the quoted sentence is what you hear; really its pieces join, with no change of sound, into the thing heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song is the signature tune played over a television programme's opening credits.

clue.text: Bless courageous and enthusiastic review

indicators.note: read the opening word as a letter followed by less, meaning without that letter

parts.note: brave means courageous
read as B-less: the letter B, which is to be taken away

explanation.surface: A critic blesses a bold work with a glowing write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bless' must be split as B-less: take B away from the word for courageous.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a highly favourable notice from a critic.

clue.text: Creation's first computer? It's made of cartilage

parts.note: Adam was the first man of the Creation in Genesis, with the possessive kept
Apple is the computer maker

explanation.surface: A quip about the very first computer at the Creation, then a straight anatomy fact.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke of a biblical figure owning a Mac.
explanation.definitionFit: The laryngeal prominence in the neck is a projection of thyroid cartilage, popularly named after the biblical first man.

clue.text: Audacity is going astray amid uneven retreat

indicators.note: amid places the word for straying in the middle of the other piece
to retreat is to go backwards, so the preceding word is read backwards

parts.note: an uneven number is odd
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Boldness strays off course during a ragged withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun for a hideaway; it is a verb acting on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic daring or boldness, the quality of audacity.

clue.text: Unfinished Hershey's candy in broken pinata from Southern Asian

indicators.note: in puts the shortened sweet inside the rearranged letters
a broken object is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Hershey's Kisses are drop-shaped American chocolates

explanation.surface: A half-eaten chocolate inside a smashed party piñata.
explanation.walkthrough: A piñata is a candy-filled papier-mâché figure broken open at parties, which makes the candy inside it natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakistan is a country of South Asia, so a person or thing from there comes from Southern Asia.

clue.text: Current tune: "Word Salad"

indicators.note: a salad is a toss-up of mixed ingredients, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A topical song title, as if a hit single were called 'Word Salad'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word salad' is a phrase for incoherent speech, but here 'Salad' tosses the letters of the two words beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a current beneath the surface moving opposite to the surface water.

clue.text: Hannah or Bob or Sarah beginning to dislike European city

parts.note: Sarah Palin, former Alaska governor and 2008 vice-presidential candidate

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of dislike
the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A list of people's names, one of whom starts to dislike a city in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of first names suggests people, but Hannah and Bob are named for reading the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both names read identically forwards and backwards, so each is an example of such a word.

clue.text: Uninitiated primate is able to produce a nut

indicators.note: uninitiated, read as lacking its initial, means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an ape is a primate
can means is able

explanation.surface: A naive monkey manages to crack open a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is the edible nut of a hickory tree native to North America.

clue.text: Overlook potassium in drink

indicators.note: in tells you the element sits inside the word for drink

parts.note: a sip is a small drink
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: Advice to ignore the potassium content in a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to pass over or omit it, a synonym of overlook.

clue.text: Solo cat chasing soft ghost

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the earlier pieces come after the later one

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
Han Solo, the Star Wars smuggler
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A lone cat stalks a gentle spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' looks like 'alone'; it gives the first name of the Star Wars character.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is an apparition or spectre, a synonym of ghost.

clue.text: Choice of brew when leaders have changed places

indicators.note: the two leading letters swap positions with each other

parts.note: a potion is a brewed drink

explanation.surface: Picking a different tea or coffee after the bosses swapped jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of the alternatives available to pick, so a choice.

clue.text: Complained (that is, moaned) at first snippet of ancient wisdom

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the preceding word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of moaned

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled on encountering a scrap of old philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes 'that is, moaned' look like a gloss on complained, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem, 'seize the day', is a Latin maxim from the poet Horace.

clue.text: Deity's male disciples making noodles

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
a god's followers are his men

explanation.surface: A god's followers prepare a noodle dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramen are Japanese wheat noodles served in broth.

clue.text: Bum's low church

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A down-and-out's humble church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective, as in Low Church; it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum is American slang for scrounging off others, which is what to mooch means.

clue.text: Where B is a dish: in Italy

parts.note: in the alphabet B comes after the first letter
taken as written; B lies beyond this letter

explanation.surface: A puzzling question of where some B counts as food in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Where is B? Past A, in alphabetical order, so the two parts join to name the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the staple Italian food of noodles and shapes made from durum-wheat dough.

clue.text: Grotesque magenta badge

indicators.note: something grotesque is distorted and misshapen, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: the colour name, used as letters

explanation.surface: A garish purplish-pink badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a label worn on clothing showing who you are, a kind of identifying badge.

clue.text: Sulfuric acid or calcium permanganate in the West, they say

indicators.note: they say means the answer matches how a phrase is pronounced, not its spelling

parts.note: the Occident is the western world

explanation.surface: Chemistry chatter about which strong acids and salts are used in Western countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Both chemicals are strong oxidising agents, examples of substances that accept electrons from others.

clue.text: Start to watch anyone but Martina on the tennis court, feeding regressive monk's willful ignorance

indicators.note: feeding means putting food into something, so these letters go inside the other word
regressive means going backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of watch

parts.words: anyone but Martina on the tennis court
parts.note: anyone but Martina Hingis, the Swiss tennis champion, read as 'not Hingis'

explanation.surface: Someone watching every tennis player except Martina, with a backward monk resolutely refusing to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: Navratilova is the Martina who comes to mind first; only Hingis, inserted after 'NOT', gives the needed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Know-Nothings were a nativist US party of the 1850s; the term now names a deliberate refusal to learn or know.
